# Easy Meals recipe library

146 recipes, including household recipes and adaptations from linked publishers. Ingredient quantities use four portions; whole-bird recipes round up to complete batches. Keto bases are shown without family starch; separate measured per-person options accompany shared recipes. Missing source quantities and nutrition are unreported. Adaptations have not been kitchen-tested.

## Lemon salmon and asparagus

4 adult servings · US imperial measures · keto · 8 min active per base batch · 25 min

Lemon salmon with asparagus and garlic.

No mid-cook action; remove fish and asparagus separately at their endpoints.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

Then: Asparagus basket: spread without a dense pile; air fry at 390°F for 7–10 min, check at 7 min; remove when ready.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.48 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Half to asparagus; half to salmon.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>½ tsp</strong> Garlic powder<small class="trn-state-detail">Divide equally.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the proportional split described in the method.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.06 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Hemp hearts<small class="trn-state-detail">hulled · Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Skin-on salmon fillets — raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick. Choose individual fillets about 170 g (6 oz) each, keeping the stated thickness.

- 1 lb Asparagus — trimmed, medium stalks

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half to asparagus; half to salmon.

- 1 tsp Garlic powder. Divide equally.

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.07 oz Lemon zest — finely grated. Use finely grated zest.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers with room for four fillets in one basket and 454 g asparagus in the other

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss asparagus with half the oil, half the garlic, and half the salt. Spread in one basket without a dense pile.

2. **Cook.** Pat salmon dry. Rub with remaining oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and zest. Put skin-side down in the other basket with gaps between fillets. Start both together.

3. **Finish.** Check asparagus at 7 minutes; medium stalks usually need 7–10. Check salmon at 10 minutes; allow 10–14 to reach 145°F. Remove each when ready. Finish with lemon juice and hemp.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 6–8 min. Toss and load separate baskets; preheat overlaps prep.

- Air fry together: 7–14 min. Check asparagus at 7 min and salmon at 10 min; remove each separately.

- Finish: 2 min. Check fish at 145°F; add lemon and hemp.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Lemon brightens the salmon; hemp adds a mild nutty finish without another cooking step.

- Thin asparagus needs an earlier check.

- Keep the fillets skin-side down and apart.

If either basket cannot hold its full batch, use two half-sheet pans at 425°F: fish about 12–18 min, asparagus 10–15 min; allow 25–35 min total.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 468 kcal; protein: 39.0 g; total carbs: 6.0 g; fiber: 2.7 g; net carbs: 3.3 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: fish. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Basket fit and actual thickness can change the time; first cook has not been kitchen-tested.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

Smoky chicken thighs with roasted broccoli.

Start broccoli five minutes after chicken; shake broccoli once.

Then: Broccoli basket: start 5 min after chicken; air fry at 390°F for 10–14 min, shake once halfway; stems fork-tender, crowns lightly browned.</td><td rowspan="5" colspan="1" class="trn-operation">Finish cooked broccoli with lemon juice and nutritional yeast.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.48 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Half to broccoli; half to chicken.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the proportional split described in the method.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.53 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="2" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.28 oz</strong> Nutritional yeast<small class="trn-state-detail">flakes · Add after cooking.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick

- 1 lb Broccoli florets — about 1½ inches across

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half to broccoli; half to chicken.

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Dried oregano

- ¾ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Add after cooking.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers with uncrowded baskets

- Instant-read thermometer

- Separate raw-poultry bowl and clean serving tools

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 390°F. Toss broccoli with half the oil and one third of the salt; load one basket without crowding. In a separate bowl coat chicken with the remaining oil and salt, paprika, garlic, oregano, and pepper.

2. **Cook.** Put unfolded thighs smooth-side up in the other basket without overlapping. Start chicken. Five minutes later, start broccoli.

3. **Finish.** Shake broccoli once halfway through its 10–14-minute cook. Chicken usually needs 16–22 minutes; check the thickest pieces for 165°F. No chicken flip is required, though the underside browns less. Finish broccoli with lemon and nutritional yeast. Broccoli is ready when stems are fork-tender and crowns are lightly browned; time alone is not its endpoint.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load chicken: 7–9 min. Start chicken first; preheat overlaps prep.

- Start broccoli: 5 min after chicken. Load broccoli basket.

- Cook: Chicken 16–22 min; broccoli 10–14 min. Shake broccoli once halfway; check chicken thickest pieces for 165°F.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lemon and yeast after cooking.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Smoked paprika and oregano season the thighs while lemon and yeast sharpen the broccoli after cooking.

- Chicken underside browns less without a flip.

- Keep yeast out of the fryer to avoid scorching.

If baskets cannot hold the batch, use two oven pans at 425°F for about 20–25 min; allow 35–40 min total and check chicken for 165°F.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 317 kcal; protein: 37.9 g; total carbs: 9.5 g; fiber: 3.8 g; net carbs: 5.7 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: none listed; check every product label. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Smaller fryer baskets require the oven fallback or extra batches.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

Pesto cod with zucchini.

One scheduled fish-pan addition, then separate vegetable/fish endpoint checks.

The listed pan and basket capacity, cook times, and thermometer endpoint are for four servings.

Ingredients are scaled; keep food thickness, spacing, settings and safe endpoints fixed. Timings assume the four-serving batch and specified shortcuts. More food can require additional batches.

Weights converted from volume or counts are approximate (~); the original measure follows in parentheses. Counts, packages and undefined measures stay as written when no reliable weight is available. US cups and spoons are US customary measures, not British Imperial. oz means mass; fl oz means volume. Substitute at most 2 g net carbs per 30 g.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>1.5 lb</strong> Zucchini<small class="trn-state-detail">sliced into ½-inch half-moons</small></th><td rowspan="4" colspan="2" class="trn-operation">Toss ½-inch zucchini half-moons with oil, salt and pepper; spread on separate pan. Then: Zucchini pan: roast at 425°F for 18–23 min; check at 18 min of zucchini cooking; browned edges and tender center.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Olive oil<small class="trn-state-detail">as purchased · Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>¼ tsp</strong> Fine salt<small class="trn-state-detail">Use the measured salt in the zucchini seasoning.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>to taste</strong> Black pepper<small class="trn-state-detail"></small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.53 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="3" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.71 oz</strong> Hemp hearts<small class="trn-state-detail">hulled · Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Cod fillets — raw, thawed; individual fillets about 1 inch thick. Choose individual fillets about 170 g (6 oz) each, keeping the stated thickness.

- 1.5 lb Zucchini — sliced into ½-inch half-moons

- 1.59 oz DeLallo basil pesto — squeeze-bottle, as sold. Weigh the scaled amount; do not infer tablespoons from the unusual label volume. Substitute at most 2 g net carbs per 30 g.

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Three quarters to zucchini; remainder to fish.

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the measured salt in the zucchini seasoning.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch rimmed metal half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss zucchini with three quarters of the oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on one half-sheet pan. Pat fish dry, rub with the remaining oil, and place on the other pan.

2. **Cook.** Start the zucchini pan first. After 6 minutes, add the fish pan. Check zucchini from 18 minutes of its own cooking time for browned edges and a tender center; allow about 18–23 minutes. Check fish after 12 minutes of its own cooking time; allow about 12–18 minutes to reach 145°F. Remove each pan at its endpoint and serve promptly. If either needs longer, keep checking; do not overcook the fish to match the vegetables.

3. **Finish.** Spoon pesto over cooked fish. Finish fish and zucchini with lemon and hemp. Applying pesto after cooking keeps its basil flavor and avoids burning the sauce.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load zucchini: 10–12 min. Preheat overlaps prep; fish and zucchini get separate pans.

- Give zucchini a head start: 6 min. Add fish pan after 6 minutes: one scheduled main-appliance action.

- Finish both pans: Fish 12–18 min; zucchini 18–23 min total roast. Check zucchini for browned edges and tenderness; fish must reach 145°F. Remove separately at their endpoints.

- Finish: 2 min. Spoon pesto on fish; add lemon and hemp and serve promptly.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Separating wet zucchini keeps cod from steaming in vegetable liquid; pesto stays fresh when added after heat.

- The six-minute vegetable head start reduces the fish holding time; doneness still decides when each pan comes out.

- Pesto goes on after cooking to protect basil flavor.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 328 kcal; protein: 33.9 g; total carbs: 7.1 g; fiber: 2.3 g; net carbs: 4.8 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: fish, milk, tree-nuts. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Pesto substitution needs no more than 2 g net carbs per 30 g to preserve the keto estimate.

- Two-pans and conventional bake are assumed.

- Pesto may contain tree nuts or other allergens; verify the specific jar label. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

- The six-minute head start is a design adjustment, not a tested synchronization guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

Base batch is 1 tsp + 1 tbsp.</small></th></tr><tr><th scope="row" colspan="1" class="trn-ingredient"><strong>0.53 oz</strong> Lemon juice<small class="trn-state-detail">unsweetened</small></th></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 12 count Large eggs — as purchased

- 2.67 fl oz Water — potable. Mix into the eggs.

- 1 lb Frozen chopped spinach — package weight before thawing and squeezing. Heat according to package directions, cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a sieve. · Buy 1 × 16 oz (454 g) packages; measure out the required weight.

- 2.65 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1.41 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Mix into eggs.

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the measured salt in the egg mixture; feta adds salt too.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.63 oz Olive oil — as purchased. One quarter for dish; three quarters for salad. Base batch is 1 tsp + 1 tbsp.

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Equipment

- Oven at 375°F on bake

- Microwave for spinach

- 9-inch square metal baking dish at least 2 inches deep

- Instant-read thermometer

- Scaling: at six or eight servings use two matching 9-inch square metal dishes, dividing the mixture to preserve original depth; oven loading can increase total time. At two servings the thinner layer may finish earlier; check the center without blindly halving the timer.

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 375°F. Heat spinach in the microwave according to its package during preheating, then let it cool until safe to handle and press very dry in a fine-mesh sieve with a spoon. Do not squeeze hot spinach with bare hands. Use one quarter of the oil to grease one 9-inch square metal dish for two or four servings, or two matching dishes for six or eight; each must be at least 2 inches deep.

2. **Cook.** Whisk eggs, water, garlic, salt, and pepper. Stir in squeezed spinach, feta, hemp, and yeast. Divide between the selected dishes so the mixture is no deeper than the original four-serving layer.

3. **Finish.** For the original four-serving layer, bake about 25–30 minutes; for the thinner two-serving layer, begin checking at 18 minutes, until the center is set and reaches 160°F. Toss greens with the remaining oil and lemon during baking. Rest the frittata for 3 minutes before cutting into the selected number of equal adult portions.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat, thaw, and mix: 12–15 min. Microwave spinach per package, cool enough to handle and press dry while preheating; oil dish and whisk mixture. Cooling or thawing delays can add time.

- Bake: 25–30 min. No mid-cook action; make salad during bake. Check center for 160°F.

- Rest and serve: 3 min. Cut into the selected number of equal adult portions.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Dry spinach prevents a watery center; feta, hemp, and yeast add savory depth.

- Squeezing spinach very dry matters more than extending the bake.

- Package spinach weight is before squeezing; drained nutrient retention is uncertain.

- Feta can use animal rennet. For a vegetarian version, check for vegetarian or microbial rennet; the generic cheese label is not verified here.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 408 kcal; protein: 30.3 g; total carbs: 9.9 g; fiber: 5.0 g; net carbs: 4.9 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Actual spinach drain and center cook time need a first cook.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

- Allow 40–50 minutes; safe spinach handling, thawing and pressing can extend prep. Two servings bake in a thinner layer: start checking the center at 18 minutes rather than assuming the four-serving time.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

- [FoodSafety.gov safe minimum temperatures](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures)

- [Bob's Red Mill nutritional yeast label](https://www.bobsredmill.com/product/nutritional-yeast)

Sauté first, then quick release after 5 minutes; stir in cream and kale.

### Ingredients

- 6.42 oz Chicken Italian sausage — raw, casings removed. No pork; check the label for allergens and fillers.

- 2.36 oz Turkey bacon — chopped

- 0.78 oz Onion — diced

- ¼ tsp Crushed red pepper — flakes

- 0.14 oz Garlic — minced

- 26.04 fl oz Chicken broth — thin, water-based

- 6.03 oz Cauliflower florets — bite-size

- 3.35 oz Organic heavy cream — added after pressure cooking

- 1.48 oz Kale — stems removed, chopped. Kale, not spinach.

- ¼ tsp Xanthan gum. Optional thickener; not counted in nutrition.

- to taste Parmesan — grated. Optional garnish; not counted in nutrition.

### Equipment

- Instant Pot 6QT or larger

- Instant-read thermometer

- Ladle

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Dice the onion, mince the garlic, chop the turkey bacon and kale, and cut cauliflower into bite-size florets. Remove sausage casings. Keep raw sausage, its board and utensils away from the kale and cream.

2. **Sauté.** Set the Instant Pot to Sauté. Brown the sausage, breaking it up, with the turkey bacon. Add the onion and crushed red pepper and cook until the onion softens. Add the garlic for about 30 seconds. Turn Sauté off.

3. **Cook.** Add the broth and scrape up browned bits so the pot does not trigger a burn warning. Add the cauliflower. Seal, switch Keep Warm off, and cook at high pressure for 5 minutes. Stay under PC MAX.

4. **Finish.** Quick release according to your manual, keeping clear of steam; vent in short bursts if the soup sputters. Open only after the float valve drops. Check the sausage reaches 165°F. Stir in the cream and kale until the kale wilts. Sprinkle in xanthan while stirring if you want a thicker soup. Serve with Parmesan if using.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare and sauté: about 12 min. Brown sausage and turkey bacon, then onion, red pepper and garlic.

- Pressurize: 10–15 min expected. Deglaze with broth before sealing; Keep Warm off.

- Pressure cook: 5 min high pressure. Countdown starts after pressure is reached.

- Release and finish: about 5 min. Quick release, open after the float drops, then stir in cream and kale.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Chicken sausage and turkey bacon replace pork, and cauliflower stands in for potatoes to keep the soup keto.

- Deglaze thoroughly after sautéing to avoid a burn warning.

- Add cream only after pressure cooking.

- Kale wilts in the hot soup; no extra cooking needed.

- Xanthan thickens quickly; sprinkle it in while stirring to avoid clumps.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 220 kcal; protein: 12.7 g; total carbs: 7.5 g; fiber: 1.8 g; net carbs: 5.6 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- 35–45 min is a planning estimate; pressure build time varies with liquid volume and starting temperature.

- Follow your exact model’s liquid minimum, PC MAX, venting and float-valve instructions. Do not leave the operating cooker unattended.

- Nutrition uses USDA smoked Italian turkey sausage as the closest poultry Italian sausage profile, excluding its outlier iron value; check your sausage, bacon and broth labels.

- Household version scaled from a 10-serving batch; not kitchen-tested at other serving counts.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, cut into 1-inch pieces

- 1 lb Cauliflower florets — about 1 inch across

- 0.95 oz Olive oil

- 2 tsp Ground cumin

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Ground turmeric

- ¼ tsp Ground cinnamon

- ¾ tsp Fine salt

- to taste Black pepper

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 5.29 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

### Family starch options (per non-keto adult)

- Cooked rice: 2.82 oz Cooked rice — fully cooked, ready to heat. About ½ cup per non-keto diner; heat ready-cooked rice. Buy at least 320 g for four.

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 60 g pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for ready-to-eat family rice or briefly warmed pita, if serving non-keto diners

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Prepare cucumber and greens. Mix yogurt with its garlic, a pinch of salt and half the lemon juice. Toss cauliflower and chicken with their own oil and spice portions and half the remaining salt on separate 18×13-inch pans.

2. **Cook.** Roast for 18–23 minutes, checking the largest chicken pieces for 165°F and cauliflower for tenderness. If your oven browns unevenly, swap racks halfway.

3. **Finish.** Near the end of roasting, if serving non-keto diners, microwave ready-to-eat rice or briefly warm the chosen pita according to its package. Assemble greens, cucumber, chicken and cauliflower. Add the prepared yogurt sauce and remaining lemon. Put starch on family plates only.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Prepare cold sides and seasoned yogurt sauce first; split remaining spice oil between cauliflower and chicken.

- Roast: 18–23 min. Check largest chicken pieces for 165°F and cauliflower for browned edges and tenderness; optional rack swap if browning unevenly. Heat ready family starch near serving.

- Finish: 2 min. Assemble with prepared yogurt sauce and remaining lemon; starch on family plates only.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Warm spices coat small chicken pieces and cauliflower; cold lemon yogurt balances them.

- Cut chicken into 1-inch pieces; no marinade wait.

- Keep ready-to-eat greens away from raw-poultry tools.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 339 kcal; protein: 39.7 g; total carbs: 11.6 g; fiber: 3.8 g; net carbs: 7.8 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Family starch adds calories and carbs only to the plates that receive it.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed; strips about 1 inch wide, no more than ¾ inch thick

- 10.58 oz Bell pepper — sliced into ¼-inch strips. Buy by the scaled edible weight; produce size varies.

- 2.12 oz Onion — sliced into ¼-inch strips. Buy by the scaled edible weight; produce size varies.

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half of spiced oil on vegetables; half on chicken.

- 2 tsp Mild chili powder blend

- 1 tsp Ground cumin

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- 1.06 oz Lime juice — unsweetened

- 5.01 oz Shredded lettuce — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

- 5.29 oz Avocado flesh — sliced; flesh weight

- 2.12 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

### Family starch options (per non-keto adult)

- Corn tortillas: 2 count Corn tortillas — ready to eat; warm according to package. Two 6-inch tortillas totaling about 50 g per non-keto diner; check the package for wheat or gluten cross-contact. Serve alongside the bowl or fill with part of the filling; two small tortillas will not hold the whole meal.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for family tortillas

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Prepare lettuce and avocado first. Mix oil, spices, and salt. Toss peppers and onion with half the mixture. Coat chicken separately with the rest.

2. **Cook.** Divide chicken and vegetables between two half-sheet pans in a single layer, keeping pieces apart. Bake about 18–22 minutes, until the largest chicken strips reach 165°F. No stir is needed if there is enough space; swap racks halfway if needed for your oven.

3. **Finish.** Finish with lime. Make keto bowls with lettuce, filling, avocado, and yogurt. Near the end of cooking, if serving non-keto diners, heat tortillas in the microwave according to their package for family portions; keep them wrapped until serving. Serve the measured two tortillas alongside each family bowl or fill them with part of the mixture; the full bowl portion is larger than two small tacos.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Prepare lettuce and avocado before raw poultry; separate chicken and vegetables on pans.

- Roast: 18–22 min. Check largest chicken strips for 165°F; swap racks if needed. Heat tortillas during cook.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lime; assemble measured keto bowls and separate family tortillas.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Roasting spaced strips concentrates pepper flavor; lime, avocado, and yogurt round out the bowl.

- Measured peppers, onion, avocado, and yogurt preserve the stated keto nutrition.

- Keep pieces separate so they roast rather than steam.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 378 kcal; protein: 37.5 g; total carbs: 13.0 g; fiber: 5.9 g; net carbs: 7.1 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Chili powder blends vary by brand and allergen label; inspect package.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

flesh weight</small></th><td rowspan="1" colspan="2" class="trn-operation">Slice avocado.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, separated and unfolded

- 375 mL minimum (measure by volume) Low-sodium chicken broth — thin, water-based. 375 mL base minimum for Instant Pot Duo 6QT; use your model’s minimum.

- 4.37 oz Herdez mild salsa verde — jarred, added after cooking. Substitute at most 2 g total carbs per 31 g; add only after pressure cooking.

- 1 tsp Ground cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- 1.06 oz Lime juice — unsweetened

- 1 lb Shredded cabbage — plain, no carrots or dressing

- 5.29 oz Avocado flesh — diced; flesh weight

- 2.12 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

### Family starch options (per non-keto adult)

- Cooked rice: 2.82 oz Cooked rice — fully cooked, ready to heat. About ½ cup per non-keto diner; heat ready-cooked rice. Buy at least 320 g for four.

### Equipment

- Instant Pot Duo 6QT covered by Duo V5 manual

- Clean board and shredding forks

- Instant-read thermometer

- Microwave for ready-to-eat family rice, if serving non-keto diners

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Put the broth, cumin, garlic, and separated thighs in the Duo 6QT. Leave salsa out. Seal, switch Keep Warm off, and set high pressure for 8 minutes. The broth amount is the 6QT minimum; follow your model’s higher minimum if required and stay under PC MAX.

2. **Cook.** During pressurization, prepare avocado and mix cabbage with yogurt and half the lime. If serving non-keto diners, leave ready-to-eat family rice for microwave heating near serving, according to its package. Keep cold sides away from raw-poultry equipment.

3. **Finish.** When pressure cooking ends, leave the valve at Seal for 10 minutes. Then vent according to your manual, keeping clear of steam. Open only after the float valve drops. Check the thickest thighs for 165°F. If needed, finish cooking in the liquid and recheck; that adds time.

4. **Serve.** Lift onto a clean board and shred. If safely cooked thighs resist shredding, slice or chop them rather than forcing a longer cook for texture alone. Mix with salsa, remaining lime, and only enough broth to moisten. Divide over slaw with avocado. Near serving, if needed, microwave family rice per package and add only to family bowls. Reserve excess broth; no reduction is required.

### Attention timeline

- Load and pressurize: 3 min load + 10–15 min expected pressure build. Broth, spices, thighs only; seal and turn Keep Warm off. Make slaw during build; heat ready family rice near serving.

- Pressure cook: 8 min high pressure. Countdown starts after pressure is reached.

- Release: 10 min natural + about 2 min controlled vent/check. Leave sealed for 10 min; vent per manual, open only after float drops. Probe thighs for 165°F.

- Shred and plate: about 6 min. Shred on clean board, or slice safely cooked thighs if resistant; mix salsa, lime and only enough broth to moisten. Heat ready family rice near serving.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Salsa after pressure cooking keeps its tang and meets the cooker’s need for thin liquid during pressure buildup.

- Keep salsa out of the pressure phase so the thin broth meets the cooker minimum.

- Keep raw-poultry gear away from cold slaw.

- Reserve excess broth; no reduction needed.

- The slaw is lightly dressed rather than creamy. Toss thoroughly and allow it to sit during cooking; check the first-cook texture before changing yogurt or lime amounts.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 327 kcal; protein: 38.6 g; total carbs: 13.9 g; fiber: 5.5 g; net carbs: 8.4 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- 40–45 min is an expected planning estimate, not a hard bound. The manual permits pressure building up to 30 min, which can make the same meal about 59 min.

- Follow your exact model’s liquid minimum, PC MAX, venting, and float-valve instructions. Do not leave the operating cooker unattended.

- Custom 8+10 timing and shreddability need a first cook.

- Check chicken broth and salsa labels for allergens; the listed milk allergen comes from yogurt. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb 93%-lean ground turkey — raw

- 1 count Large egg — as purchased. For fractional eggs, beat whole eggs and weigh 50 g per large-egg portion; half an egg is about 25 g.

- 0.49 oz Ground flaxseed — ground, not whole. Ground seed acts as a binder; whole seeds are not equivalent.

- 1.76 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.16 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Lightly oil baskets.

- 10.58 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Family starch options (per non-keto adult)

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 60 g pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. Serve pita alongside both patties and salad.

- Bun: 1.59 oz Bun — ready to eat; warm briefly. One 45 g ready-to-eat bun per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. The bread accompanies both patties; use a double-patty bun or serve the second patty beside it.

### Equipment

- Two air fryers, each with roughly 8×8 inches usable flat space for four patties

- Instant-read thermometer

- Clean board and serving tools

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Preheat both fryers to 380°F. Prepare cucumber, greens, and yogurt mixed with lemon first. Mix turkey, egg, flax, feta, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper just until combined. If the scaled egg amount is half an egg, beat one whole egg and use half by weight, about 25 g.

2. **Cook.** Form patties about 100 g each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick; allow about two per adult. Oil baskets lightly. In the four-serving batch, put four patties in each only if they fit with gaps; about 8×8 inches of usable flat space per basket is a starting fit check. Do not cram them in.

3. **Finish.** Cook about 14–18 minutes, flipping once halfway, until each patty reaches 165°F. If serving non-keto diners, warm the chosen family bread during cooking. Serve patties with cucumber, greens, and yogurt sauce. A family bun is one double-patty serving, or put one patty in the bun and the other beside it; pita goes alongside the full plate.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare and form: 10–12 min. Prepare cold sides first; mix lightly and form patties roughly 100 g each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick.

- Air fry: 14–18 min. Four patties per basket only if gaps remain; flip once halfway, check each for 165°F. Warm one bread choice during cook.

- Serve: 2 min. Two patties per person with cucumber, greens, and yogurt.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Ground flax binds the turkey; feta and lemon yogurt keep a lean patty from tasting flat.

- Ground flax binds; whole flax is not equivalent.

- Do a cold basket fit check before committing to air frying.

If patties do not fit with gaps, bake on half-sheet pans at 425°F for about 18–22 min; check every patty for 165°F. Four-serving base batch can fit on one pan; larger batches may need more pans or rounds. Allow 35–40 min for the base batch.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 378 kcal; protein: 39.9 g; total carbs: 7.7 g; fiber: 2.3 g; net carbs: 5.4 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Patties may require the oven fallback in smaller fryers.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 11.99 oz Fully cooked chicken breast — plain, refrigerated, chopped no larger than ¾ inch. Already fully cooked; raw chicken is not a substitute.

- 1.06 lb Canned cooked lentils — drained and rinsed. Drained weight; canned yield varies. · About 2 × 15 oz (425 g) cans, assuming ~240 g drained per can; check actual yield.

- 14.5 oz Canned diced tomatoes — with juice, room temperature. do not drain. · Buy 1 × 14.5 oz (411 g) cans; measure out the required weight.

- 5.01 oz Baby spinach — roughly chopped

- 0.48 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Mix into the bake.

- 1 tsp Smoked paprika

- 1 tsp Ground cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ½ tsp Dried oregano

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 2.12 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- 13×9-inch shallow metal baking dish

- Foil cover

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. In a 13×9-inch shallow metal baking dish, mix lentils, tomatoes, spinach, oil, spices, and salt. Fold in cooked chicken. Spread and gently press to an even layer no more than 1 inch deep; split into two shallow dishes if needed.

2. **Cook.** Cover tightly with foil. Bake about 20–25 minutes. Check the center and several chicken pieces for 165°F; continue if needed.

3. **Finish.** Finish with lemon and feta, then divide into the selected number of equal adult portions. This is a moist bake.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and mix: 10–12 min. Mix in shallow dish; keep depth no more than 1 inch, split dishes if needed. Cover tightly.

- Bake: 20–25 min. Check center and several chicken pieces for 165°F.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lemon and feta; divide equally.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

A tight foil cover and tomato liquid keep precooked chicken moist while lentils heat through.

- Covered tomato liquid protects cooked chicken from drying.

- This is moist, not a crisp tray bake.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 380 kcal; protein: 41.4 g; total carbs: 30.8 g; fiber: 12.6 g; net carbs: 18.2 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Do not substitute raw chicken, dry lentils, or frozen chicken blocks.

- First cook should log depth, starting temperatures, and time to 165°F.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.06 lb Canned chickpeas — drained, rinsed, patted dry. Drained weight; canned yield varies. · About 2 × 15 oz (425 g) cans, assuming ~240 g drained per can; check actual yield.

- 1.5 lb Cauliflower florets — about 1 inch across

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Mix with harissa.

- 2.12 oz Mina mild harissa — jarred. Measured Mina mild harissa; half for roasting and half for yogurt. Hot concentrated pastes are not equivalent.

- 1 tsp Ground cumin

- ½ tsp Garlic powder. For yogurt sauce.

- ½ tsp Fine salt. Half for roasting and half for the yogurt sauce.

- to taste Black pepper. To taste in yogurt.

- 1.32 lb Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix oil, half the harissa, cumin and half the salt. Toss thoroughly dried chickpeas and cauliflower with it. Spread across two half-sheet pans without crowding.

2. **Cook.** Roast for about 22–25 minutes, stirring once and swapping racks halfway, until cauliflower is tender and browned. Chickpeas should still be soft inside.

3. **Finish.** During roasting, mix yogurt with the remaining harissa and salt, lemon, garlic and pepper. Divide all the yogurt evenly among the selected number of plates, then add greens and roasted ingredients. Finish with hemp. This uses the specified mild harissa; hotter concentrated pastes do not inherit the same quantity or nutrition.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Dry rinsed chickpeas; toss with cauliflower, oil, half the mild harissa, cumin and half the salt; spread over two pans.

- Roast: 22–25 min. Stir once and swap racks halfway. Mix yogurt with remaining mild harissa/salt, lemon, garlic and pepper during cooking.

- Assemble: 2 min. Divide the full scaled yogurt amount equally among plates; add greens, roast, and hemp.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Cumin-roasted cauliflower and soft-centered chickpeas meet a cold lemon-harissa yogurt sauce. Splitting the mild harissa between roast and sauce keeps some pepper flavor out of the oven; a little salt seasons the full yogurt portion.

- The full scaled strained-yogurt amount is required for the stated protein per adult.

- Chickpeas should remain soft inside.

- Pat chickpeas dry with a clean towel before seasoning; wet surfaces steam instead of browning. The doubled mild-harissa dose is a design improvement that still needs tasting.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 426 kcal; protein: 28.8 g; total carbs: 45.4 g; fiber: 12.0 g; net carbs: 33.4 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Ordinary yogurt or omitted yogurt changes protein and calories.

- Mina mild harissa label underlies nutrition; concentrated alternatives need a new calculation.

- Check harissa and yogurt labels for additional allergens. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

- For six/eight servings preserve the original single-layer spacing with extra pans or base-size batches. Original cook times apply to the original four-serving batch; more pans or rounds can extend total time.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw, thawed, unfolded; no more than ¾ inch thick

- 1.25 lb Baby potatoes — cut no larger than ¾ inch

- 1 lb Green beans — trimmed

- 0.95 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Half to potatoes; one quarter each to beans and chicken.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ¾ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.07 oz Lemon zest — finely grated. Use finely grated zest.

- 1.06 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.28 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Add after cooking.

- 1.01 fl oz Water — potable. Microwave steaming water; drain before roasting.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Microwave about 1000 W

- Vented microwave-safe dish

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Put potato pieces and water in a microwave-safe dish with a vented microwave-safe cover. Microwave on high for about 6–8 minutes in a roughly 1000 W microwave, until just fork-tender, then carefully uncover and drain. Prepare the rest during this step.

2. **Cook.** Before handling raw chicken, mix the oil, oregano, garlic, zest and pepper in a clean bowl. Give half to the drained potatoes, one quarter to beans and one quarter to chicken in separate bowls; give each one third of the salt. Spread potatoes over one half of a half-sheet pan, reserving the other half for beans. Set beans aside. Put unfolded chicken on the second pan. Keep the vegetable portion and tools away from raw-poultry juices.

3. **Finish.** Roast chicken and potatoes for 20–25 minutes. Add green beans to the vegetable pan after the first 10 minutes, keeping them in a separate area rather than piling them over potatoes. Swap racks at that addition. Chicken must reach 165°F; potatoes and beans should be tender. Remove each when ready.

4. **Serve.** Finish with lemon juice. Sprinkle yeast over vegetables after cooking.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and microwave: 12–16 min. Microwave potatoes with the measured water until just fork-tender; drain carefully. Prep chicken and beans during this stage.

- First roast: 10 min. Potatoes on half a vegetable pan; chicken on second pan.

- Add beans and finish: 10–15 min. Add beans to reserved area and swap racks; check chicken for 165°F and vegetables for tenderness.

- Finish: 2 min. Add lemon; sprinkle yeast over vegetables.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

The same lemon, garlic and oregano oil seasons the chicken and both vegetables. The microwave head start makes the potatoes tender before roasting, and delayed beans keep their texture. Lemon and yeast finish the dish after the hot oven.

- Keep beans and potatoes in separate single-layer areas.

- Skipping microwave step lengthens roasting.

- Check that the full bean portion fits the reserved half-pan without a dense pile. An extra pan or rounds can add time; record this fit on the first cook.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 422 kcal; protein: 39.6 g; total carbs: 34.8 g; fiber: 6.8 g; net carbs: 28.0 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: none listed; check every product label. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Microwave head start of 567 g potatoes at about 1000 W is an untested estimate; fork-tender endpoint controls.

- Smaller pans can require extra batches.

- Check every packaged ingredient label for additional allergens; this data is not an allergy guarantee.

- Microwave load and heating time do not scale linearly; for six/eight servings microwave potato portions in separate base-size loads until fork-tender, allowing extra elapsed time.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb DeLallo potato gnocchi — shelf-stable, not frozen. Buy 1 × 16 oz (454 g) packages; measure out the required weight.

- 1.06 lb Canned cannellini beans — drained and rinsed. Drained weight; canned yield varies. · About 2 × 15 oz (425 g) cans, assuming ~240 g drained per can; check actual yield.

- 1 lb Broccoli florets — about 1½ inches across

- 10.58 oz Cherry tomatoes. Buy by the scaled edible weight; produce size varies.

- 1.43 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Two thirds for first roast; one third with beans midway.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- ½ tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.14 oz Nutritional yeast — flakes. Add after cooking.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

- 0.71 oz Hemp hearts — hulled. Use hulled hemp hearts in the measured portion.

- 3.53 oz Pre-grated Parmesan — as sold. Required for stated protein; check rennet label if vegetarian food is needed.

### Equipment

- Oven at 425°F on bake

- Two 18×13-inch half-sheet pans

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss gnocchi, broccoli, and tomatoes with two thirds of the oil, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper. Divide across two half-sheet pans. Do not boil gnocchi first.

2. **Cook.** Roast for 12 minutes. Toss beans with the remaining oil. Add them to the pans, stir everything once, and swap racks. Continue roasting for about 13–18 minutes, until gnocchi are tender inside and broccoli is tender and browned.

3. **Finish.** At the finish, press a few softened tomatoes with the serving spoon and toss their juices through the gnocchi and beans. Toss in yeast, lemon and half the Parmesan while warm; divide equally into the selected number of adult portions and top with the remaining Parmesan and hemp. The full measured Parmesan is included in the nutrition.

### Attention timeline

- Preheat and load: 10–12 min. Toss shelf-stable unboiled gnocchi, broccoli and tomatoes with two thirds of the measured oil and seasoning; spread on two pans.

- First roast: 12 min. No stirring yet.

- Add beans and finish: 13–18 min. Toss drained beans with the remaining oil; add, stir all once, swap racks. Cook until gnocchi centers and broccoli are tender.

- Finish: 2 min. Press a few softened tomatoes and toss their juices through the gnocchi and beans; incorporate the measured finishes, with all Parmesan divided among plates.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Roasted shelf-stable gnocchi stays tender inside; later beans avoid drying, while Parmesan supplies protein.

- The full scaled Parmesan amount is required for the stated protein per adult.

- Animal rennet is possible in Parmesan; this recipe is plant-forward and is not labeled vegetarian without checking the specific cheese.

- Adding beans halfway helps avoid dry beans.

- Tomato juices help the warm cheese and yeast coat the food instead of sitting on top as dry powder; do not keep roasting after the gnocchi centers are tender.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 604 kcal; protein: 26.7 g; total carbs: 81.4 g; fiber: 11.8 g; net carbs: 69.6 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: milk, wheat. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Other brands, fresh or frozen gnocchi, and gluten-free products can change timing and nutrition.

- USDA canned white bean proxy lacks an explicit drained-state qualifier; this is an approximation.

- Check the gnocchi label for egg, soy, and other allergens. This data is not an allergy guarantee.

- For six/eight servings preserve the original single-layer spacing with extra pans or base-size batches. Original cook times apply to the original four-serving batch; more pans or rounds can extend total time.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb 93%-lean ground turkey — raw

- 1 count Large egg — as purchased. For fractional eggs, beat whole eggs and weigh 50 g per large-egg portion; half an egg is about 25 g.

- 0.49 oz Ground flaxseed — ground, not whole. Ground seed acts as a binder; whole seeds are not equivalent.

- 1.76 oz Crumbled feta — as sold. Cheese label and rennet vary.

- 1 tsp Dried oregano

- 1 tsp Garlic powder

- ¼ tsp Fine salt. Use the proportional split described in the method.

- to taste Black pepper

- 0.16 oz Olive oil — as purchased. Divide among batches.

- 10.58 oz Cucumber — diced

- 5.01 oz Salad greens — washed, ready to eat. Buy by scaled edible weight.

- 4.23 oz Plain strained Greek yogurt — plain, strained. At least 9 g protein and no more than 4 g total carbs per 100 g.

- 0.53 oz Lemon juice — unsweetened

### Family starch options (per non-keto adult)

- Pita: 2.12 oz Pita — ready to eat; warm briefly. One ready-to-eat 60 g pita per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. Serve pita alongside both patties and salad.

- Bun: 1.59 oz Bun — ready to eat; warm briefly. One 45 g ready-to-eat bun per non-keto diner; warm briefly. Contains wheat; check package. The bread accompanies both patties; use a double-patty bun or serve the second patty beside it.

### Equipment

- Stovetop and 12-inch nonstick frying pan

- Instant-read thermometer

- Mixing bowl

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Mix yogurt with lemon. Prepare cucumber and greens. Mix turkey, egg, flax, feta and seasoning just until combined. Form about two patties per serving about 100 g each, 3¼ inches across and ¾ inch thick.

2. **Pan-fry.** Heat a 12-inch nonstick frying pan over medium heat. Divide the oil among batches. Add oil and up to four patties at a time. Cook 5–6 minutes per side, until every patty reaches 165°F. Repeat until all patties are cooked.

3. **Serve.** Serve two patties per person with cucumber, greens and lemon yogurt. Serve the selected bread alongside.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare: 10–12 min. Mix sauce and form patties.

- Pan-fry two batches: 20–24 min. Turn once per batch and check each patty for 165°F.

- Serve: 2 min. Plate two patties with salad and yogurt.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Ground flax binds the turkey; feta and lemon yogurt keep a lean patty from tasting flat.

- Mix turkey lightly to keep patties tender.

- Use a nonstick pan and divide the measured oil between batches.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 378 kcal; protein: 39.9 g; total carbs: 7.7 g; fiber: 2.3 g; net carbs: 5.4 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: egg, milk. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Larger servings require more batches.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- 0.49 oz Olive oil

- 1.41 oz Onion — diced

- 0.53 oz Garlic — minced

- 1.06 oz Red bell pepper — diced. The old optional pepper is included in this estimate.

- 0.11 oz Fine salt. Original amount; reduce to taste if your broth or sauce is salty.

- 9.98 oz Red enchilada sauce — ready-to-eat, canned. Base four-serving batch: about one 10 oz can. Estimate uses Old El Paso medium red sauce; labels vary.

- 0.11 oz Cayenne pepper. Original amount is very hot. Start with less if desired.

- 14.99 oz Canned white beans — fully cooked, including can liquid. Base four-serving batch: one 15 oz can; do not substitute dry beans.

- 32.46 fl oz Reduced-sodium chicken broth — ready-to-use

- 14.11 oz Cooked shredded chicken breast — fully cooked, skinless, boneless; cooked edible weight. Added in the restored version because the old Chicken Posole entry omitted a chicken amount.

- 0.53 oz Lime juice

- 5.29 oz Cabbage — finely shredded. Measured amount for the old to-taste garnish.

- 0.28 oz Cilantro — washed and chopped. Measured amount for the old to-taste garnish.

### Equipment

- Stovetop and 4-quart or larger saucepan; larger pot or batches for six/eight servings

- Spoon and clean chopping board

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Prepare.** Use fully cooked shredded chicken and canned, fully cooked beans. Wash and prepare the vegetables and garnishes. Set a 4-quart or larger saucepan on the stovetop; use a larger pot or batches for six or eight servings.

2. **Sauté.** Heat the oil over medium heat. Cook onion and bell pepper for about 5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

3. **Simmer.** Add broth, enchilada sauce, canned beans with their liquid, salt and cayenne. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the cooked chicken and return to a simmer. Heat until chicken reaches 165°F in several places, about 5 minutes or longer as needed. Do not use raw chicken with this method.

4. **Finish.** Turn off the heat and stir in lime juice. Divide among four bowls and top with cabbage and cilantro. Taste before adding more salt or cayenne.

### Attention timeline

- Prepare and sauté: 10–15 min. Chop vegetables; soften onion and pepper, then briefly cook garlic.

- Boil and simmer: 15–20 min. Bring broth, sauce and beans to a boil; simmer 10 min, stirring occasionally.

- Heat chicken and finish: 5 min or longer to 165°F. Add fully cooked chicken, check temperature, then add lime and garnishes.

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Red enchilada sauce gives the broth chile flavor; lime and fresh cabbage balance it.

- The original recipe used beans, not hominy. This restores that version rather than a traditional pozole.

- The source gave no pressure time. This adaptation uses a saucepan, not pressure cooking.

- The original 3g cayenne is hot; use less to suit your taste.

### Nutrition per serving

Calories: 376 kcal; protein: 43.0 g; total carbs: 32.6 g; fiber: 6.7 g; net carbs: 25.9 g

Per adult: base includes measured sauces, seeds and sides. Family nutrition adds one selected starch portion. US net carbs = total carbohydrate − fiber. Labels and food variation matter; no guarantee of ketosis.

Known allergens for these plates: none listed; check every product label. Check product labels and cross-contact.

### First-cook checks and limits

- Restored from the old Chicken Posole recipe. Its oil, onion, garlic, pepper, salt, sauce, cayenne, beans, broth and lime amounts are retained.

- The source omitted chicken and a cooking time. The 400g cooked chicken and stovetop method are new; cabbage and cilantro now have measured garnish amounts. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.

- Nutrition uses generic USDA ingredients, canned white beans including liquid, and an Old El Paso sauce label with an estimated 60g per quarter cup. Broth is modeled at 1g/mL. Brands, draining beans, and reducing garnishes or seasoning change the estimates.

- Complete micronutrient totals are unavailable for this restored recipe and are omitted. Check chicken, broth and sauce labels for allergens.

### Leftovers

Refrigerate in shallow containers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F. Keep cold greens and yogurt separate.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ tbsp Butter

- ⅔ tbsp Minced garlic

- ⅔ count Jalapeño — seeded and chopped

- ⅔ cup Unsweetened almond milk

- ⅙ cup Heavy cream

- 2 oz Cream cheese

- 2.67 oz Canned green chilis — undrained. Two-thirds of the source four-ounce can at four servings.

- ⅔ tsp Chili powder

- ⅔ tsp Ground cumin

- ⅓ tsp Onion powder

- ⅔ cup Shredded cheddar for the sauce

- 3 ⅓ cup Shredded chicken — fully cooked

- ⅓ cup Shredded cheddar for topping

### Equipment

- Stovetop and large lidded skillet

- Whisk and spoon

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Start the sauce.** Set a large skillet over medium heat. Melt the butter, then stir in the minced garlic and seeded jalapeño for about 30 seconds.

2. **Melt the cheeses.** Whisk in almond milk, cream, cream cheese, undrained chilis, chili powder, cumin, onion powder and the sauce portion of cheddar. Keep stirring until the sauce is smooth.

3. **Heat the chicken.** Fold in the fully cooked chicken. Scatter the topping cheddar over it, cover, and turn the heat to low. Simmer for about 10 minutes; confirm the chicken reaches 165°F in several places before serving.

### Attention timeline

Stages can overlap; endpoints and appliance behavior override the estimate.

### Flavor and capacity

Green chilis, cumin and jalapeño season the creamy cheddar sauce.

- Keep the two cheddar portions separate until topping.

### Ingredients

- 8 count Boneless skinless chicken thighs — raw

- ½ cup G Hughes Sugar Free Honey Mustard

- 1 lb asparagus — tough ends removed

- ½ cup sliced bell pepper

- ¼ cup sliced red onion

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- to taste salt and pepper to taste. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed.

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Arrange.** Put chicken at one end of the sheet and season it. Coat with half the honey mustard.

2. **Vegetables.** Arrange the asparagus, pepper and onion at the other end. Mix butter with garlic, drizzle over the vegetables and season to taste.

3. **Roast.** Bake 20–25 minutes, until chicken reaches 165°F internally.

4. **Glaze.** Brush chicken with the remaining mustard. Broil 2–3 minutes, watching the glaze closely.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb Chicken — raw; cut into chunks

- 1 tsp cumin

- 1 tsp chili powder

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp onion powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 cup bell pepper — cut into small pieces

- ½ cup onion — cut into small pieces

- 2 count jalapeños — seeded and diced

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- ⅓ cup chicken broth

- 2 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup cheddar — divided

- 1 tbsp Olive oil or cooking spray. Source method allows up to 1 tablespoon olive oil OR unmeasured nonstick spray. This measured amount is an upper limit, not a mandatory minimum.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Season.** Mix cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken in this blend.

2. **Brown.** Warm a large skillet over medium heat with the source method's spray or oil. Sear chicken 2–3 minutes per side. Add peppers, onion and jalapeños, then cook about 5 minutes, until the vegetables begin softening. Transfer everything to a plate.

3. **Sauce.** Over medium-low heat, melt the listed butter into cream, broth, cream cheese and half the cheddar; stir until thickened.

4. **Finish.** Return the chicken and vegetables, scatter the remaining cheddar on top and cover. Simmer on low for 6–8 minutes, checking the chicken reaches 165°F.

### Ingredients

- 4 count small chicken breast — this was about 1.5 pounds for me. Source says 4 small chicken breasts, approximately 1.5 pounds total.

- 1 tsp cumin

- ½ tsp chili powder

- ½ tsp garlic powder

- ½ tsp salt

- ½ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp butter

- ½ cup chopped onion — half of one small onion

- 2 count jalapenos — seeded and diced

- 1 tsp minced garlic

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- ⅓ cup chicken broth

- 2 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese — divided

- 1 tbsp Olive oil or cooking spray. Source method allows up to 1 tablespoon olive oil OR unmeasured nonstick spray. This measured amount is an upper limit, not a mandatory minimum.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Season.** Combine the spices and coat both faces of each chicken breast.

2. **Sear.** Warm the skillet over medium with the source spray or oil. Brown the chicken 2–3 minutes per side, then transfer it to a plate.

3. **Sauce.** Melt the butter in the pan; sauté onion, jalapeños and garlic for 3–4 minutes. Lower the heat, pour in cream and broth, and stir in cream cheese until smooth. Melt half the cheddar into the sauce.

4. **Finish.** Return chicken, cover it with the remaining cheddar, then put on the lid. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked.

### Ingredients

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 lb chicken breast — cut into cubes

- 1 tsp garlic powder

- 1 tsp onion powder

- ½ tsp paprika

- ¼ tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 5 cup broccoli florets

- 1 tbsp butter

- 1 tsp garlic

- 1 cup unsweetened almond milk

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- 3 oz cream cheese

- 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese

- ½ cup shredded cheddar cheese

### Equipment

- Oven-safe skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Warm the skillet over medium. Cook cubed chicken in the first butter portion with the dry spices for 5–6 minutes, browning all faces. Set chicken aside.

2. **Cheese sauce.** In the same pan, heat the second butter portion, garlic, almond milk, heavy cream, cream cheese and sauce cheddar. Whisk as the cream cheese melts.

3. **Bake.** Fold chicken and broccoli into the sauce. Add topping cheddar and bake 20–25 minutes. Wait 10 minutes before serving so the sauce can thicken.

### Ingredients

- ¼ cup gluten free soy sauce

- 1 tbsp rice vinegar

- 2 tbsp brown sugar swerve — or other keto friendly sweetener

- 2 tbsp sesame oil

- 2 tsp minced garlic

- 1 tbsp olive oil or sesame oil for frying

- 1.5 lb chicken — thinly sliced

- 1 count medium size zucchini — sliced

- to taste salt and pepper to taste. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed.

- 2 tbsp cashews — chopped

- 2 tbsp green onions — chopped

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Sauce.** Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, sweetener, sesame oil and garlic together.

2. **Stir-fry.** Heat the frying oil in a skillet over medium. Season chicken to taste and brown it for 5–6 minutes. Stir in zucchini and cook another 2–3 minutes.

3. **Simmer.** Coat the contents with the prepared sauce. Cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes. Add the listed chopped cashews and green onions when serving.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts — pounded to an even thickness

- 1 tsp Italian seasoning

- to taste salt and pepper — to taste. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed.

- 1 tbsp butter

- 2 tbsp butter — divided

- 1 tsp minced garlic

- 8 oz Mushrooms — thinly sliced; source uses one 8-ounce package

- ½ cup white cooking wine — or chicken broth

- ¼ cup heavy cream

- 2 slice Swiss cheese — halved

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Sear.** Coat chicken with Italian seasoning and salt and pepper. Melt the first butter portion in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Sear chicken 3–4 minutes on each face, then reserve it; it will finish cooking later.

2. **Mushrooms.** Use half the divided butter portion to cook garlic and mushrooms with wine or broth. Simmer until nearly all the liquid evaporates.

3. **Finish.** Stir in the rest of the divided butter and the cream. Return chicken and place halved Swiss slices over it. Cover and simmer for 6–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb thin cut chicken breasts

- 1 tsp salt

- ¼ tsp pepper

- 1 tbsp unsalted butter

- 1 cup chicken bone broth — or chicken stock

- 4 clove garlic — minced

- 4 cup cauliflower — rice or chopped small

- 1 tbsp fresh thyme

- 2 tbsp heavy cream

- 1 tbsp lemon juice

- 1 tsp lemon zest — from 1 lemon

- Not specified Fresh thyme — garnish, optional. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed. Optional; excluded or included as stated in the publisher nutrition.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Season chicken with salt and pepper. Brown it in butter over medium-high heat for 3–5 minutes, turn, then cook 2–4 minutes more to an internal 165°F. Transfer to a plate and tent with foil.

2. **Cauliflower.** Pour broth into the skillet and add garlic and cauliflower. Loosen the browned residue from the pan and simmer 4–5 minutes until cauliflower is just tender.

3. **Finish.** Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in thyme, cream, lemon juice and zest. Return chicken and add optional thyme garnish.

### Ingredients

- ⅔ cup Greek Yogurt

- ⅔ tbsp Ginger paste

- 2 clove Garlic, minced

- ⅔ tsp Kosher salt

- ⅓ tsp Black pepper

- 1.33 lb Boneless skinless chicken thighs cut into bite size chunks

- 1 ⅓ tbsp avocado oil

- ⅔ tsp Kosher salt

- 2 ⅔ clove Garlic, minced

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Ginger paste

- 1 ⅓ tsp Garam Masala

- 1 ⅓ tsp Smoked paprika

- 5.33 oz Tomato sauce — source uses one 8-ounce container

- 1 ⅓ tbsp Tomato paste

- ⅓ cup Heavy cream

- 2 tbsp Butter

- Not specified Fresh cilantro for garnish. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed. Optional; excluded or included as stated in the publisher nutrition.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Stir yogurt, marinade ginger, marinade garlic, first salt portion and pepper together. Coat chicken and refrigerate for 1 hour.

2. **Cook.** Heat the listed avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken through to 165°F, about 8 minutes. Pour off liquid released by the chicken and marinade so the sauce stays thick.

3. **Sauce.** Stir in the remaining garlic, ginger and salt, plus garam masala and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute. Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, cream and butter; cook a few minutes until thickened.

4. **Serve.** Add the optional cilantro garnish. Cauliflower rice is a serving suggestion rather than a measured part of this recipe.

### Ingredients

- 1.5 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs

- 2 count large bell peppers

- 1 lb zucchini

- 2 tbsp olive oil

- 1 lemon Lemon juice — juice from one medium lemon

- 2 tbsp Red wine vinegar. Source misspells tablespoons as tablespoona.

- 1 tsp sea salt

- ½ tbsp dried oregano

- 1 tsp dried dill

- 1 tsp garlic powder

### Equipment

- Oven

- Baking sheet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Marinate.** Whisk oil, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, oregano, dill and garlic powder together. Coat chicken with half this marinade and refrigerate for 20 minutes or overnight. Keep the other half separate for vegetables.

2. **Arrange.** Place marinated chicken in the middle of the sheet. Put vegetables around it and toss them with the reserved marinade.

3. **Bake.** Roast at 450°F for 25 minutes. Verify chicken reaches 165°F in its thickest part; return to the oven if needed. The source also says to check after 3 minutes, which conflicts with its stated bake time.

### Ingredients

- 1 lb Boneless skinless chicken breasts — raw; slice horizontally into thin fillets. Source says 2–3 breasts, about 1 pound. Uses its explicit weight basis. Source range: 1–1 lb; use the lower stated amount as the scaled starting point.

- to taste salt and pepper — to taste. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed.

- 2 tbsp olive oil

- 2 tbsp butter

- 2 cup sliced mushrooms

- ½ cup Marsala wine

- ½ cup chicken broth

- 1 cup heavy whipping cream

- 1 tsp ground mustard

- 1 tsp garlic powder

- Not specified Chopped Parsley for garnish. Source does not state an amount; measure to taste or as needed. Optional; excluded or included as stated in the publisher nutrition.

### Equipment

- Lidded skillet

- Mixing bowl

- Instant-read thermometer

### Cook

Prepare cold sides first. Keep raw-poultry tools separate; use clean serving utensils. Probe more than one thick piece. A timer is not a doneness test.

1. **Chicken.** Season the chicken to taste. Warm half the oil and all the butter in a large skillet over medium. Fry chicken 3–4 minutes on each side until cooked. Keep it on a plate under foil.

2. **Mushrooms.** Add the remaining oil and sauté mushrooms 2–3 minutes. Pour in Marsala; bring to a boil and reduce for 3–4 minutes.

3. **Sauce.** Stir in broth, cream, mustard and garlic powder. Bring back to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.

4. **Finish.** Return chicken for 1–2 minutes to warm it in the sauce. Serve with optional parsley.
